title: Retiam Engine Performance & Zero-GC Optimization Guide

blocks.content: Engineering notebook from `docs/PERFORMANCE_OPTIMIZATIONS.md`. This archive preserves the project’s original rationale, equations, performance reports and illustrative code. Historical paths, API names, claims and sketches can differ from the current engine. For copy-ready programs use the guides and demos; for current callable signatures use the source-derived API. Performance figures here describe reported experiments, not guaranteed frame rates.

blocks.text: Original document: [docs/PERFORMANCE_OPTIMIZATIONS.md](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/docs/PERFORMANCE_OPTIMIZATIONS.md). See [current limitations](/limitations) for concrete compatibility notes.

This document details the architectural changes, memory management strategies, and algorithm optimizations implemented to achieve **Zero Garbage Collection (0.0 KB Minor GC)** and **sub-millisecond CPU frame times (< 0.05 ms)** across complex scenes (e.g. 30,000+ vector paths in Paris 30K).

blocks.text: A. True Zero-Copy Persistent Retained Slot Allocation

items: **Files:** [`src/engine/render/allocator/GlobalStateAllocator.ts`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/render/allocator/GlobalStateAllocator.ts), [`src/engine/_core/StateDataManager.ts`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/_core/StateDataManager.ts), [`src/engine/_core/Entity.ts`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/_core/Entity.ts)

blocks.text: Previously, `GlobalStateAllocator` functioned as a per-frame linear bump allocator (`resetForNewFrame()` reset allocation head to 0). Each frame, `traverse()` allocated slot $0 \dots N$ sequentially and copied 64 float values from `entity._cachedWorldState` into the staging buffer via `Float32Array.set()`. In a 30,000-entity scene, this transferred **1.92 million floats (~7.68 MB) every frame**, causing high CPU memory traffic.

children: Each entity is assigned a permanent slot (`_stateSlotIndex`) in `GlobalStateAllocator` via `acquireSlot()`.
Slices in `GlobalStateAllocator.cpuData` map directly to `entity.worldState`.
When an entity is destroyed, its slot is recycled back into `_freeSlots`.
When an entity or parent moves, `worldState.apply(entity.state, parentState)` writes directly into `cpuData` in-place.
When an entity is static, **zero memory operations occur**.
On buffer geometric growth ($2\times$), `cpuData.set(oldData)` preserves existing float states, and `_initMappedStates(0, newCap)` remaps all active states.

blocks.text: B. Hierarchical State Version Memoization (parentId + childId Cache)

items: **Files:** [`src/engine/_core/State.ts`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/_core/State.ts), [`src/engine/_core/Transform.ts`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/_core/Transform.ts), [`src/engine/_core/Paint.ts`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/_core/Paint.ts), [`src/engine/_core/Material.ts`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/_core/Material.ts), [`src/engine/_core/SceneComposer.ts`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/_core/SceneComposer.ts)

blocks.text: In deeply nested hierarchy trees, calculating `worldState.apply(entity.state, parentState)` executes 4×4 matrix multiplications (`mul()`), translation additions, paint color blending, and material overrides on every node every frame, even when no object in the scene has moved.

children: Every `State`, `Transform`, `Paint`, and `Material` tracks an integer `version` incremented on mutation.
`State.localVersion` computes the composite hash of all local components.
In `SceneComposer.traverse()`:

items: If neither the parent world matrix nor the entity's local transform/style has changed, the evaluation is **completely bypassed**.

blocks.text: C. Scene-Level Render Queue & GPU Buffer Caching

items: **Files:** [`src/engine/_core/SceneComposer.ts`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/_core/SceneComposer.ts)

blocks.text: When the user orbits, pans, or zooms the camera (e.g. via `CameraController` or `OrbitCameraController`), the scene graph objects are completely static, yet the engine was rebuilding the entire render command queue and re-uploading the 7.68 MB storage buffer to the GPU.

items: Added `_sceneGraphDirty` tracking to `SceneComposer`.
When only the camera moves, `prepare()` updates view projection uniforms, reuses `_cachedCommands`, and skips `buildRenderQueues()`, `traverse()`, and `stateManager.uploadToGPU()`.
CPU frame time during camera interaction drops from **~8.0 ms to < 0.05 ms (600+ FPS)**.

blocks.text: D. CPU Update Loop & Subtree Culling (childUpdateCount)

items: **Files:** [`src/engine/_core/Entity.ts`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/_core/Entity.ts), [`src/engine/_core/Scene.ts`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/_core/Scene.ts)

blocks.text: Composite entities (such as SVGs containing 30,000 static child paths) were recursing through all 30,000 nodes inside `Entity.update()`, calling empty component update hooks and invoking `.forEach()` closure callbacks that generated **32.7 MB of Minor GC nursery allocations**.

children: Entities track how many descendant nodes have active `updaters` or custom component `update()` methods.
When `_childUpdateCount === 0`, `Entity.update()` early-outs immediately in $O(1)$, skipping all 30,000 children.
Replaced all `Array.forEach(...)` with indexed `for` loops across `Entity.ts`, `Scene.ts`, and `SceneComposer.ts`.

items: **Files:** [`src/engine/utils/Raycaster.ts`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/utils/Raycaster.ts), [`src/engine/_core/Entity.ts`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/_core/Entity.ts)

blocks.text: During `pointermove` events, `Raycaster.cast()` walked every single child node in the scene, allocating stack items and executing ray-AABB tests across 30,000 non-interactive vector paths.

items: Added `_childPickableCount` with parent notification in `Entity.ts`.
`Raycaster.cast()` checks `node.isPickable || node._childPickableCount > 0` before pushing child nodes to the traversal stack, pruning 30,000 non-pickable SVG paths at the root level in $O(1)$.

blocks.text: F. Zero-Allocation getDrawCalls() & Geometry Rendering Pipeline

items: **Files:** All geometry classes under [`src/engine/components/geometry/`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/components/geometry) and [`src/engine/components/renderers/`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/components/renderers)
`TriangulatedPathGeometry.getDrawCalls()` was clearing its array (`length = 0`), querying singletons, and re-pushing `DrawCall` objects 30,000 times per frame.

Other geometry classes (`Geometry2D`, `QuadGeometry`, `CircleGeometry`, `PolyGeometry`, `IndexGeometry2D`, `TextGeometry`, `LineGeometry`, `ModelGeometry`, `MorphGeometry`) returned inline literal arrays `[{ vertexCount: ... }]`, creating tens of thousands of temporary arrays per frame.
Pre-built `_cachedDrawCalls` inside `_updateDrawCalls()` in `TriangulatedPathGeometry.ts`, updating it **only when geometry is triangulated or modified**.
Made `getDrawCalls()` an instant, zero-allocation reference return (`return this._cachedDrawCalls;`).
Replaced inline literal arrays across all geometry classes with persistent retained array slots.

blocks.text: G. WebGPU Scissor Rect & State Caching

items: **Files:** [`src/engine/render/RenderStateCache.ts`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/render/RenderStateCache.ts), [`src/engine/render/passes/RenderPass.ts`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/render/passes/RenderPass.ts)

blocks.text: `RenderPass.execute` was issuing `pass.setScissorRect(...)` for every single entity packet in the render queue, generating **30,000 WebGPU API calls per frame**.

items: Added scissor rectangle caching to `RenderStateCache.setScissorRect(pass, x, y, w, h)`.
Consecutive packets sharing identical scissor bounds skip the WebGPU driver call, reducing scissor commands from 30,000 to **1 per frame**.
`RenderStateCache.reset(device)` cleanly invalidates cached pipeline and scissor states at the start of each render pass encoder.

**Files:** [`src/engine/_core/State.ts`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/_core/State.ts), [`src/engine/utils/gpu_utils.ts`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/utils/gpu_utils.ts)

blocks.text: The legacy alignment helper `round(n, base)` was written as `n + (base - (n % base))`. When $n = 256$ (already aligned to 16 bytes), $256 \pmod{16} = 0$, producing **272 bytes (68 floats)** for standalone `State` instances, while `GlobalStateAllocator` sub-arrays were fixed at **256 bytes (64 floats)**. Copying between them triggered `RangeError: offset is out of bounds`.

items: Replaced rounding with standard `Math.ceil(n / base) * base`, guaranteeing exact **256 bytes (64 floats)** across the entire engine.
Updated `State.copyFrom(state)` to safely handle exact or sliced array sets.

blocks.text: Chrome / Edge DevTools Flame Chart Evolution

children: **Minor GC:** 29.7 MB – 32.7 MB per frame.
**Bottlenecks:** `RenderPass.execute`, `Entity.update` traversal, `Raycaster.cast` on pointer move.
**Minor GC:** Dropped to 0.0 kB.
**Scripting Time:** Dropped to ~8.0 ms (dominated by matrix multiplication `apply() -> mul()`).
**Scripting Time:** Dropped to ~1.0 ms.
**Bottleneck Identified:** Repeated `copyFrom()` (1.92M floats copied into bump allocator).
**Minor GC:** **0.0 kB (Permanently Zero GC)**.
**`copyFrom` Calls:** **0 (Completely Eliminated)**.
**`getDrawCalls` Latency:** **< 0.001 ms**.
**Total Frame CPU Time:** **< 0.05 ms (600+ FPS capable)**.

blocks.text: 5. Best Practices for Retiam Engine Development

items.text: **Retain Object & Array Allocations in Hot Paths:**
children: Never use inline array/object literals (`[{ ... }]`, `{ ... }`) in `getDrawCalls()`, `getPasses()`, `update()`, or `render()`.
Pre-allocate scratchpads and cached arrays on class instances.
Avoid `Array.prototype.forEach`, `.map`, `.filter` in per-frame update and render loops to prevent closure instantiations.

When modifying custom entity properties that impact GPU rendering, bump the component's `version` or call `entity.invalidate()` to trigger coalesced GPU streaming without forcing full scene graph re-evaluations.
